svg.title: Fabric Streaming Analytics: Hot and Cold Paths from One Event Stream
svg.desc: An architecture flow starting at event sources feeding into Eventstream, which routes and shapes events with built-in stream-processing operators. From there the flow splits: the hot path lands events in an Eventhouse KQL database for indexed, low-latency query and native anomaly detection, feeding Activator rules that fire alerts and automated actions, and Real-Time Dashboards for live monitoring. The cold path uses OneLake availability to write the same KQL table data into Delta format with adaptive batching, making it queryable by lakehouse, warehouse, Spark, and Power BI Direct Lake without any copy. A warning node covers the DDL operations blocked while OneLake availability is enabled, and a feedback edge shows Activator triggering Fabric jobs that write back into the lakehouse cold path.

g.title: Event sources — Kafka, Kinesis, Pub/Sub, MQTT, CDC feeds, and other streaming producers.
g.text: Streaming Analytics Pattern — End-to-End Event Flow on Microsoft Fabric

g.title: Eventstream — No-code ingestion, shaping, and routing to multiple destinations simultaneously.
g.text: Sources → Eventstream (route/transform) → Eventhouse hot path & OneLake cold path → Activator + Real-Time Dashboards / Power BI

g.title: Eventhouse KQL database (hot path) — Indexed, low-latency store organized by arrival time, with native anomaly detection.

g.text: Live time-series, in place, no copy

g.title: OneLake availability (cold path) — Adaptive batching writes the same KQL table data into Delta Parquet, no separate pipeline.

g.aria-label: Trap: DDL operations blocked under OneLake availability
g.title: Trap: DDL operations blocked under OneLake availability — Renaming, retyping, RLS, and row deletes are blocked while OneLake availability is active on a table.

g.text: KQL data exposed in Delta Lake format
No data movement · no extra storage charge
Delay: up to 3 h default, min 5 min

g.title: Activator — Monitors live conditions and fires notifications, automations, or Fabric job executions.
Lakehouse / Warehouse / Power BI (cold-path consumers) — Cross-engine reporting and joins over the OneLake-available Delta data.
